# What goes here

A spec is a proposed change: what it is for, what was decided, and the order of work. `docs/specs/` holds every spec:
being written, in progress, or closed. Open problems go in `docs/backlog/`, and what was done in `docs/log.md`. Start
from [index.md](index.md).

# One spec

One spec is one file, `docs/specs/<slug>.md`. The slug never changes once the file exists, because commit messages,
other documents and the `epic` of other specs refer to it. The frontmatter holds the fields used for filtering.
Everything else goes in the body.

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Spec` |
| `title` | Display name |
| `description` | One sentence: what the spec changes |
| `tags` | Exactly one area, one of the `areas` declared in `.config/rotproof.toml`. The index groups specs by it, in that order |
| `status` | `draft` (not agreed yet), `stable` (agreed) or `deprecated` (closed) |
| `epic` | Optional. The slug of the spec this one is a part of. See "Epics" |

The body is free, except that a closed spec opens with `# Resolution`: its first heading.

# Writing and closing

- **A spec describes the current state.** When it disagrees with the implementation, fix it in the same commit. A
  rejected design left looking current is read as correct by the next reader.
- **Closing a spec leaves it where it is.** Set `status: deprecated` and write `# Resolution` as its first heading:
  implemented or dropped, and how the implementation differs from the spec. A reader who opens it from a link meets
  the closing before anything that reads as current. From then on it is history. The index lists it under `# Closed`.
  A spec never moves: a moved spec breaks every link to it, and rewriting the links puts lines that have nothing to do
  with the closing into its review.
- **Links between documents are markdown links.**

# Areas

An area says where a spec belongs, and never closes. A spec that cannot name one area mixes two: split it into one
spec per area, and tie them back together as parts of an epic.

# Epics

An epic says which piece of work a spec is part of, and closes when the work is finished. It is not a document type
of its own: a spec that other specs name in `epic` is an epic, and keeps its own goals, decisions and order of work.

A piece of work is split into parts of an epic for one of two reasons: it is too large for one spec, or it spans
more than one area (see "Areas"). A spec that has grown in one area is split the same way.

- **A part names its epic by slug,** not by path. The slug names a spec in `docs/specs/`: a backlog item or a guide
  is not a spec, and a spec is not its own epic.
- **One level only.** An epic has no `epic` of its own.
- **A part may be in another area than its epic.** The area and the epic are independent.
- **An epic closes after its parts.** A closed epic has no open part. A part that is dropped instead closes as
  dropped, as any spec does. A draft part that turns out to be work of its own removes its `epic`.
- **A spec written after its epic closed is not a part of it.** The work it belonged to is finished: the new spec
  starts a new epic or stands alone, and the area connects it to the earlier work.

In an index, a part in the same area as its epic, and open or closed as its epic is, is listed under it, indented. Any
other part is listed on its own with `Epic: [<title>](...)` after its line.

# Index

[index.md](index.md) is generated: the open specs by area, then the closed ones under `# Closed`. After adding or
changing a spec, run `rotproof index`. `rotproof check` fails
when the index differs from what `rotproof index` writes.

# Differences from OKF

- `epic` is an extension field, which OKF allows. OKF expresses relations between documents with links and the prose
  around them; `epic` is a field so that Rotproof can check it. The index writes it as a link.
